summary: Verified the EmployeeComplianceModal name-matching bug-fix (frontend only). The tokens()/sameName() helper logic was unit-tested with 14 cases (case-insensitive, punctuation, middle initial w/wo dot, whitespace, false-positive prevention) and ALL 14 passed. End-to-end UI testing using the seeded training matrix 'TEST_MIDDLENAME_MATRIX' confirmed: (a) Training Matrix Records section now matches 'JOHN X. TSOUKALAS' against employee 'John Tsoukalas' and renders the rows, (b) Multi-middle name 'PETER A B CRACIUNOIU' matches 'Peter Craciunoiu', (c) Nicholas Ghanakas (no matrix entry) correctly shows 0, (d) False-positive foils 'John Doe' and 'Mary Tsoukalas' are correctly EXCLUDED from John Tsoukalas's report, (e) John X. Tsoukalas's records do NOT leak into Peter's modal. HOWEVER one regression remains: the forgiving match does NOT apply to Forklift Licenses or First Aid Certificates because those API calls send {params:{search: fullName}} and the backend pre-filters by strict substring on full name BEFORE the client-side sameName() filter runs. The seeded forklift license 'John X. Tsoukalas' was correctly returned 200 by the API but was filtered out server-side and never reached the modal (John FL=0/1).

ui_bugs.issue: Forgiving name match is NOT applied to Forklift Licenses or First Aid Certificates. The frontend sends ?search=<fullName> to /api/compliance/forklift and /api/compliance/first-aid which strict-substring-filters server-side. A forklift license stored as 'John X. Tsoukalas' is excluded before sameName() can see it, so the Compliance Report for 'John Tsoukalas' shows 0 forklift licenses. Verified by seeding TEST-FL-001 with name 'John X. Tsoukalas' via POST /api/compliance/forklift (status 200) — modal still shows '(0)' for John Tsoukalas. Fix: drop the search param for these two calls (fetch all & client-filter, mirroring the training-matrices approach), OR pass only the first token e.g. params.search='Tsoukalas' (last name) and keep client-side sameName as the final gate.
ui_bugs.selector: [data-testid='employee-compliance-modal'] section: Forklift Licenses / First Aid Certificates

action_items: Fix EmployeeComplianceModal.js so that Forklift Licenses and First Aid Certificates also benefit from forgiving name match. Easiest: remove the {params:{search: fullName}} on lines 48-49 and rely entirely on the client-side .filter(x => sameName(x.name)). Alternatively send only the last-name token. Re-test by seeding a forklift license with a middle-initial name and confirming the compliance modal for the no-middle-initial employee shows it.
critical_code_review_comments: EmployeeComplianceModal.js line 47-49: server-side `search` param defeats the new forgiving match for compliance/forklift and compliance/first-aid endpoints.

Line 77 uses `.find()` which only returns the first matching person row per matrix. If a matrix happened to list the same person twice (e.g. once with and once without middle initial) only the first occurrence's scores would be aggregated. Likely acceptable in practice but worth a code comment.
Forklift/First-Aid search param strips out partial matches before client sees them — same root cause as the original Training Matrix bug, just at a different boundary.

The 14-case sameName() unit test is reproducible via page.evaluate; copy the tokens()/sameName() snippet directly from EmployeeComplianceModal.js lines 58-69.
rca of the issue: The bug-fix correctly replaces the strict equality check (`norm(x.name) === me`) on the Training Matrix branch with a forgiving token-based comparison. The training-matrices endpoint returns full data so the client can re-filter — this works. But for forklift & first-aid, the frontend still sends ?search=<fullName> which causes the backend to apply a strict substring filter, removing middle-name variants BEFORE sameName() runs. Reproduction: as admin, POST /api/compliance/forklift with name='John X. Tsoukalas'; then open the Employee Compliance modal for 'John Tsoukalas' — Forklift Licenses shows (0). Mitigation: stop sending the search query for these two GETs (or send only the last-name token) and let sameName() be the sole filter.
